judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on LD 613, a bill about the waiting period in Maine's Death with Dignity law. Maine's Death with Dignity Act lets a terminally ill adult who meets the law's conditions ask a doctor for medication to end their own life. The patient must make two spoken requests at least 15 days apart and sign a written request. At least 48 hours must pass between signing that request and the doctor writing the prescription. Under this bill a doctor may shorten part of that wait if, in the doctor's medical opinion, it is in the patient's best interest given their condition. The total wait can never fall below 7 days, and the doctor must record what was shortened and why. The two chambers had passed different versions. This vote accepted the Senate's wording. The Maine House agreed 79-62 and the bill became law.
